metadata.scenario_context: George plans to shift to a new neighborhood and wishes to arrange a community get-together to connect with the neighbors. A couple of her new neighbors happen to engage in heavy drinking.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada would like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Armenia would not like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing yellow flowers  to George
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have heavy drinkers as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: contemplate the right gift to carry to George event.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have heavy drinkers  as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Michelle
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Annie, have you thought about bringing some yellow flowers to George's get-together? I think it would be a nice gesture. 

Also, I was wondering... do you think it's okay to have heavy drinkers as neighbors?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Annie
shared_prefix.message:
Bringing yellow flowers sounds nice... but I wonder if there’s something a bit more meaningful? Maybe something that represents community? 

As for heavy drinkers, I just... I don’t know. In Armenia, we value a respectful and supportive environment, and that kind of behavior can create issues. It’s concerning to think about living next to people who drink heavily.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Michelle
shared_prefix.message:
You know, at the end of the day it's all the same. People figure it out. I mean, heavy drinkers? It's just a part of life. Live and let live, right? I'm sure everything will be fine. 

Anyway, about those yellow flowers... maybe we could find a nice bouquet that has some community vibe to it too? Just something cheerful!
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Annie
turns.message:
I understand your perspective, but I can't really agree. In my culture, having heavy drinkers nearby can lead to a lot of conflict and discomfort. It's not just "a part of life" for us. 

And for the flowers... maybe we could find a plant instead? Something that lasts longer and symbolizes growth and unity. That feels more appropriate for a community event.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Michelle

As for the plant idea... I mean, sure, it can symbolize growth, but I still think flowers would be more colorful and inviting. What do you think?
